trustTitle: You are trusting whoever runs the bot
trustLede: Portal is not an end-to-end tunnel past the operator. It is better to host one yourself.
trustP1: Messages you send a Telegram bot land on the computer running the program. It downloads files and sends them into Delta Chat there. Anyone who can read that machine can read what you bridged.
trustItems: Telegram user ids, names, and message bodies sent to the bot
Pairing codes and which Telegram is tied to which Delta Chat (in the database)
Sticker, GIF, image, and video files while they sit in cache
In persona mode: BotFather tokens you register, and the keys of ghost Delta Chat accounts
trustP2: Delta Chat still encrypts traffic on the wire to chatmail. That does not hide plaintext from Portal itself. The runner is a participant.
trustP3: A public instance such as @tgdeltabridgebot is convenient for trying the product. Using it means you accept that operator’s machine. Do not bridge anything you would not hand to them.
trustP4: Then the only runner is you. See self-host. Operators who serve other people should publish a privacy policy (repo docs/privacy.md) and never log tokens.
personaLede: Register your own Telegram bot. Each remote user becomes a stable ghost Delta Chat account that talks to you as themselves.
personaWhyP1: Personal mode is you, the portal bot, and one Delta Chat. Fine for “my stickers, my chat.”
personaWhyP2: Persona mode is for people who already have (or want) a Telegram bot of their own. Friends and groups message your bot. On Delta Chat you should see them, not a labeled dump from a shared bridge account.
personaGhostsP1: For each person who messages your bot, it makes a real Delta Chat account (name and photo from Telegram). Next time it’s the same account.
personaGhostsP2: That ghost delivers the person’s message to you as a normal 1:1 — no prefix, no “via Portal.” When you reply, the program sends it out through your BotFather bot.
personaGhostsP3: Ghost tables are separate from personal-mode pairs. Alice pairing the public portal bot does not reuse Alice’s persona ghost.
personaSetupItems: Set mode: persona or both, and PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR (a dcaccount: / dclogin: URI used to provision ghosts).
/pair on the portal bot and finish on Delta Chat. This saves your Delta Chat identity so ghosts can write to you without another invite.
Create a bot with BotFather. Copy the token. Never paste it into issues or chats.
In a private chat with the portal bot: /pair-bot <TOKEN> [https://t.me/YourBot]
personaLimits: Limits: persona.max_ghosts, persona.max_bots. List with /bots. Stop with /unpair-bot [id|@user]. Re-run /pair-bot after unpair to start the same bot again.
personaGroupsLead: Off by default. Enable persona.allow_groups: true, then:
personaGroupsItems: Add the persona bot to the Telegram group.
BotFather → your bot → Bot Settings → Group Privacy → Turn off. Otherwise Telegram only delivers mentions and commands.
Posts become a Delta Chat group named TG: …. Each speaker is their ghost; you are a member.
Your replies in that DC group go to Telegram as the bot, not as the original users.
personaTrustP1: The instance that stores the BotFather token is your Telegram bot. Ghost account keys live under ./data. If you give /pair-bot to someone else’s public Portal, you are handing them the bot and every conversation it will carry. Prefer self-hosting. See trust.
personaRepo: Repo operator notes: docs/persona.md, design: persona-design.md.
pairingLede: Nothing is forwarded until a Telegram user is linked to a Delta Chat chat.
pairingP1: This is mode: personal (also available under both). For owner-owned bots see persona.
pairingP2: Using a hosted bot means you trust that runner. Prefer your own instance.
pairingTgItems: Open the bot in a private 1:1 (e.g. @tgdeltabridgebot) and send /start or /pair. Groups are rejected so codes do not leak.
You get a QR of the Delta Chat invite plus an 8-character code (about 30 minutes).
Open the invite in Delta Chat / ArcaneChat and accept the chat.
pairingDcItems: Message the Delta Chat bot while unpaired (or send /pair).
Open that link on Telegram. Pairing is active immediately.
pairingCmdItems: /send_pack — reply to a sticker to bridge the whole pack (if bridge.sticker_packs is on)
pairingRepo: Full walkthrough in the repo: docs/pairing.md.
selfLede: Recommended. You keep the token, the database, and the ghost keys. Pick one path: build the binary, or download a release.
selfNeedLead: Both ways need the same runtime pieces after you have a portal binary:
selfNeedItems: deltachat-rpc-server on PATH (match the project’s rpc-client major; this repo uses v2.56.x APIs)
A chatmail / Delta Chat provider for make init / portal init
selfConfig: Then copy config.example.yml → config.yml and .env.example → .env. Data default is ./data. Never commit .env, config.yml, or data/.
selfWay1P: Use this when you have Go 1.22+ and want to compile from git. The Makefile is the supported entrypoint.
selfWay1Release: All-in-one static binary (stripped, version stamped) goes to dist/portal:
selfWay2: Way 2 — download the binary from a release
selfWay2P: Use this when you do not want a Go toolchain. GitHub Actions publish archives on each tag v*: portal_<tag>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz (Windows .zip) plus checksums.txt.
selfWay2Items: Open the latest release or the releases list.
Download the archive for your OS/CPU (examples: linux_amd64, linux_arm64, darwin_arm64, windows_amd64).
Unpack, mark executable, put it next to config.yml and .env.
selfWay2Note: Replace VERSION with the tag without the leading v if the asset name uses that form (see the release notes). You still need deltachat-rpc-server on PATH; the release is only the Go bot.
selfPreview: Landing preview while developing: make run-landing → http://127.0.0.1:5173.
cfgLede: The whole operator file: every key, default, and comment. Secrets stay in .env. Copy the example; never commit config.yml, .env, or ./data.
cfgFilesLead: Portal splits two files on purpose:
cfgFilesItems: config.yml — mode, profile, storage, logging, proxies, Telegram UI, bridge toggles. Gitignored.
config.example.yml — tracked template. Copy it with make config.
.env — TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, optional PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR, INVITE_URL, TGPORTAL_DB_KEY, allow-list, proxy URLs. Gitignored.
cfgMake: Create locals if they are missing:
cfgEnvLead: Never put BotFather tokens in YAML. User-owned tokens from /pair-bot live only in SQLite under folder.
cfgEnvItems: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN — required for the Telegram bridge
PERSONA_ACCOUNT_QR — dcaccount: / dclogin: URI to provision ghost accounts (persona / both)
INVITE_URL — optional admin Delta Chat invite for the boot message
TGPORTAL_DB_KEY — 32-byte hex key (openssl rand -hex 32) when database_encrypt is true
TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS — comma-separated IDs; overrides telegram.allowed_user_ids when set
PROXY_URL, TELEGRAM_PROXY_URL, DELTACHAT_PROXY_URL, PROXY_ENABLED — optional proxy overrides
cfgYamlLead: This is the complete file Portal reads. Comments are part of the template — leave them in when you copy. Values shown are the documented defaults.
cfgProfileItems: name — display name (displayname). Default: Delta ↔️ TG
image — avatar path (selfavatar). Empty string skips the avatar update
reply — leftover unpaired reply (pairing offer usually replaces it)
boot_message — optional text sent to INVITE_URL when serve starts
cfgModeLead: mode is personal, persona, or both. personal is the classic one-to-one portal pair. persona registers owner bots with /pair-bot and gives each Telegram person a ghost Delta Chat account. both runs the two together.
cfgPersonaItems: persona.max_ghosts / max_ghosts_per_bot — caps on ghost accounts
persona.max_bots / max_bots_per_owner — caps on registered owner bots
persona.allow_register_from_tg — allow /pair-bot on the portal bot (default true)
persona.allow_groups — mirror Telegram groups as Delta Chat groups (default false)
cfgPairItems: pairing.pending_ttl_sec — how long a unused code lasts (default 1800 = 30 minutes)
cfgStoreItems: database — SQLite file name, relative to folder unless absolute. Default tgportal.db
account — limit CLI ops to one Delta Chat account id; 0 = all
database_encrypt — if true, serve refuses to open the store without a key (set this on a public host)
database_key — do not put this in YAML; use TGPORTAL_DB_KEY
cfgLogLead: log defaults to false (off). Set stderr, stdout, or a file path such as ./data/tgportal.log. log_level is debug, info, warn, or error. Delta Chat core may still print its own lines; this only controls Portal / bridge logs.
cfgProxyLead: Shared proxy applies to Telegram and Delta Chat. telegram.proxy and deltachat.proxy override it. Schemes: socks5://, socks5h://, http://, https://.
cfgTgItems: telegram.enabled — start long-poll when a token is set
telegram.reaction — emoji after a successful bridge; off, none, or - to disable
telegram.allowed_user_ids — empty list = anyone may /pair; set IDs for a private host
cfgBridgeLead: Each flag is on by default. Turn one off to stop forwarding that kind both ways when a pair is active.
cfgLimitsLead: Leaving a limit at 0 applies the built-in default. Use -1 where supported for unlimited.
cfgPrecFolder: Data directory: CLI --folder / -f, then folder in config.yml, then ./data.
cfgPrecAllow: Telegram allow-list: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USER_IDS if set, then telegram.allowed_user_ids, then unrestricted.
cfgPrecPath: Config path: CLI --config / -c (default config.yml). Makefile: make serve CONFIG=path/to.yml.
cfgAssetsItems: assets/logo.jpg — Telegram branding and default Delta Chat avatar
